deep.reconstruction:
Title (as written by H. Weber, copying Riemann; 'H Weber scrips.' at bottom right): 'Ueber Gleichgewicht der Electricität auf Cylindern mit kreisförmigem Querschnitt und parallelen Axen'.

(1) Physical reduction. Two problems are treated together:
- the distribution of static electricity on infinite cylindrical conductors with parallel generators;
- the stationary temperature in such conductors.
Riemann assumes the data are constant along lines parallel to the generators: the acting forces in the first case, the surface temperatures in the second. The problem is then two-dimensional. It is solved once the following is solved.

(2) Dirichlet problem. S is a plane, connected, schlicht (simply spread) domain bounded by arbitrary curves. Find u(x,y) with u_xx + u_yy = 0 in S and arbitrary prescribed values on the boundary. Here S is n-connected, with boundary curves C_1..C_n.

(3) Reduction to a simpler problem. Seek an analytic function zeta = xi + i*eta of z = x + i y with these properties:
- (a) zeta is real on every boundary curve C_k;
- (b) on each C_k there is exactly one point p_k where zeta has a simple pole;
- (c) otherwise zeta is finite and continuous in S.

Claimed consequences ('es lässt sich leicht zeigen'):
- (i) zeta takes every real value exactly once on each C_k;
- (ii) zeta takes every value with Im > 0 exactly n times in the interior, n being the number of boundary curves.

Implicit argument (mine): for w with Im w > 0, the number of roots of zeta = w in S is the winding number of zeta(C) about w. Each C_k is mapped monotonically onto the extended real line, passing once through infinity at p_k, so each contributes winding 1, for a total of n. For this to work the pole coefficients must have the sign that makes Im zeta > 0 near p_k inside S.

(4) The covering surface. zeta therefore maps S conformally onto an n-sheeted surface T over the upper half zeta-plane. The page breaks off here. The next page adds:
- T is bounded by the n copies of the real axis;
- T has 2n-2 simple interior branch points. This follows from Riemann–Hurwitz: chi(S) = 2-n = n*chi(half-plane) - b, so b = 2n-2.
- Doubling T by reflection gives a closed surface of genus p = n-1 with 4n-4 branch points (the Schottky double).
- Green's function of T is the imaginary part of a third-kind integral with poles at epsilon and conj(epsilon) and real periods.
- The Dirichlet problem is then solved by Green's formula u(epsilon) = -(1/2pi)∮ u d(eta)/d(nu) ds.

This page itself contains no computation, only the formulation and the reduction strategy.
errors: No computational errors on the page.

Existence of the function zeta (one simple boundary pole on each boundary curve, real on the boundary) is assumed ('Man bestimme') without proof. For an arbitrary choice of one point on each boundary curve this is a nontrivial theorem, later proved in the disk form by Bieberbach (1925) and Grunsky (1937/41).

The claims (i) and (ii), called 'leicht', tacitly require Im zeta > 0 in S. This requires a sign condition on the residues at the boundary poles relative to the orientation. The condition is not stated.

The title speaks of circular cross-sections, but this page treats arbitrary boundary curves. The circle case is the specialisation treated with the s-function / Schwarzian on the preceding page. This is an inconsistency of scope, not an error.

results.what: Reduction of 2D electrostatics/stationary heat flow for parallel infinite cylinders to the plane Dirichlet problem
results.modern_name: Dirichlet problem for the Laplace equation in a multiply connected plane domain

results.what: Existence of a function real on all n boundary curves, with one simple pole on each, mapping an n-connected domain n-to-1 onto the upper half-plane
results.modern_name: Bieberbach–Grunsky theorem / Ahlfors-type proper map of degree n (real function on the Schottky double)
results.usually_credited_to: Bieberbach 1925, Grunsky 1937-41 (disk version); Ahlfors 1950 (extremal version); Schottky 1877 (double)

results.what: The n-sheeted image T has 2n-2 branch points; its double has genus n-1 (next page)

deep.surprise_reason: This is H. Weber's copy of a Riemann Nachlass piece that Weber published in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) as 'Gleichgewicht der Electricität auf Cylindern mit kreisförmigem Querschnitt und parallelen Axen'. The anticipation of the Bieberbach–Grunsky / Schottky-double approach is therefore already known to historians. Existence is only asserted, not proved.

checkable.sympy: n,b=symbols('n b'); solve(Eq(2-n, n*1 - b), b)
checkable.asserts: Riemann–Hurwitz: n-sheeted cover of the half-plane by an n-connected domain has b = 2n-2 branch points
The double (2n sheets over the sphere, 4n-4 branch points) has genus p = n-1
n=1 case: zeta = i(1+z)/(1-z) is real on |z|=1, with a simple pole at z=1 (result 0)
n=1 case: the interior is mapped to the upper half-plane (value i at the centre), degree 1 = n

transcription_corrections: Bottom right: 'H Weber scrips.' (archival pencil note); the hand is Weber's copy, not Riemann's autograph.
Marginal numbers '28' and '27' are folio numberings, not mathematics.
'x y [?]' should read simply 'x y'; there is no further symbol.
The struck phrase after 'in' in line 2 of the problem statement is likely 'cylindrischen Leitern'; the reading is consistent with the insertion 'unendlichen' above the next line.
The inserted heading 'Das Problem' replaces the struck 'die Aufgabe'; the reading is correct.
